facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that may be a junior synonym of Sinosaurus.
facts.quote: Shuangbaisaurus (meaning "Shuangbai reptile") is genus of theropod dinosaur, possibly a junior synonym of Sinosaurus.

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus lived in the Early Jurassic of Yunnan Province, China, and is known from a single species, S. anlongbaoensis.
facts.quote: It lived in the Early Jurassic of Yunnan Province, China, and is represented by a single species, S. anlongbaoensis, known from a partial skull.

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus had a robust skull measuring 54 cm in length with a length-to-height ratio of 2.84, excluding the crests.
facts.quote: Shuangbaisaurus had a relatively robust (compared to Sinosaurus) skull, with a length of 54 cm and a length/height ratio of 2.84, not including the thin paired crests that were present at least above the eye sockets.

facts.statement: The skull crests of Shuangbaisaurus were likely formed mainly from the frontal bone, possibly including the postorbital and prefrontal bones.
facts.quote: These crests are incompletely preserved, but appeared to have been formed mostly from the frontal bone, as well as possibly the postorbital and prefrontal bones.

facts.statement: A groove separating the premaxilla and maxilla at the jaw tip is a defining characteristic of Shuangbaisaurus, also found in Sinosaurus.
facts.quote: At the tip of the jaw, the premaxilla and maxilla are separated by a groove, which is also a defining characteristic of Sinosaurus.

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus is known from a single partial skull specimen (CPM C2140ZA245) missing most of the snout, stored at the Chuxiong Prefectural Museum in Yunnan, China.
facts.quote: Shuangbaisaurus is known from a single specimen, a partial skull missing most of the top of the snout, stored at the Chuxiong Prefectural Museum in Chuxiong Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan, China under the specimen number CPM C2140ZA245.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in purple muddy siltstone in Liuna Village, Anlongbao Town, Shuangbai County, approximately 100 km south of the Lufeng deposits.
facts.quote: It was discovered in layers of purple muddy siltstone located in Liuna Village, Anlongbao Town, Shuangbai County, Chuxiong Yi, about 100 km south of the well-known Lufeng deposits.

facts.statement: The fossil-bearing layers belong to the Early Jurassic Fengjiahe Formation, tentatively dated to the Hettangian stage.
facts.quote: These layers have been recognized as belonging to the Early Jurassic Fengjiahe Formation, which has been tentatively dated to the Hettangian.

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus anlongbaoensis was formally described and named in 2017 by Wang Guo-Fu, You Hai-Lu, Pan Shi-Gang, and Wang Tao.
facts.quote: In 2017, the type and only species of the genus Shuangbaisaurus, S. anlongbaoensis, was formally described and named by Wang Guo-Fu, You Hai-Lu, Pan Shi-Gang, and Wang Tao.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to Shuangbai County and the species name to Anlongbao Town, both referencing the fossil's location.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to Shuangbai County, and the specific name refers to Anlongbao Town (with Anlongbao literally meaning "dragon-placing fort"), and thus both elements of the binomial name reference its provenance.

facts.statement: In 2019, Philip Currie and colleagues suggested that the Shuangbaisaurus specimen might fall within the variation of Sinosaurus triassicus.
facts.quote: In a 2019 conference abstract, Philip Currie and colleagues suggested that CPM C2140ZA245 fell within the range of variation of specimens assigned to Sinosaurus triassicus.

facts.statement: The vertical groove between the premaxilla and maxilla complicates Shuangbaisaurus classification, as it was previously considered a distinguishing feature of Sinosaurus.
facts.quote: However, the vertical groove separating the premaxilla and maxilla, which seems to be present in Shuangbaisaurus, was denoted as a distinguishing characteristic of Sinosaurus by Matthew Carrano and colleagues in 2012, thus complicating its referral to a new genus by Wang et al.

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus belongs to the order Saurischia.
facts.quote: ordo: Saurischia

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus belongs to the suborder Theropoda.
facts.quote: subordo: Theropoda

facts.statement: The fossil range of Shuangbaisaurus is the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Jurásico Inferior

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus anlongbaoensis is the only known species of the extinct genus Shuangbaisaurus, a dilophosaurid theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Shuangbaisaurus anlongbaoensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Shuangbaisaurus (nombre que significa "lagarto de Shuangbai") de dinosaurio terópodo dilofosáurido

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus lived during the early Jurassic period, approximately 199 to 196 million years ago in the Hettangian.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 199 a196 millones de años durante el Hettangiense

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus lived in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Asia

facts.statement: Remains of Shuangbaisaurus were found in Yunnan province, China, where only a partial skull was discovered.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en la provincia de Yunnan, en China, solo se encontró un cráneo parcial

facts.statement: Like the contemporary theropods Dilophosaurus and Sinosaurus, Shuangbaisaurus possessed a pair of thin crests in the middle of its skull.
facts.quote: Como en los terópodos Dilophosaurus y Sinosaurus, del cual era contemporáneo, Shuangbaisaurus tiene un par de crestas delgadas en el medio del cráneo

facts.statement: Unusually, the crests of Shuangbaisaurus extended backward over the level of the eyes.
facts.quote: De forma inusual, estas crestas se extendían hacia atrás sobre el nivel de los ojos

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus had a relatively robust skull compared to Sinosaurus, measuring 54 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Shuangbaisaurus tenía un cráneo relativamente robusto comparado con Sinosaurus, con una longitud de 54 centímetros

facts.statement: The crests of Shuangbaisaurus appear to have been formed mainly by the frontal bone, and possibly the postorbital and prefrontal bones.
facts.quote: Estas crestas no están preservadas completas, pero parecen haber estado conformadas principalmente por el hueso frontal, así como posiblemente por los huesos postorbital y prefrontal

facts.statement: The anteorbital fenestra of Shuangbaisaurus is large, occupying approximately one-third of the skull's length.
facts.quote: La fenestra anteorbital de Shuangbaisaurus es grande, ocupando aproximadamente un tercio de la longitud del cráneo

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus is known from a single specimen, a partial skull missing much of the upper snout.
facts.quote: Shuangbaisaurus es conocido a partir de un único espécimen, un cráneo parcial al que le falta mucho de la parte superior del hocico

facts.statement: The specimen is housed in the Chuxiong Prefecture Museum in Chuxiong Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan, China, with catalog number CPM C2140ZA245.
facts.quote: alojado en el Museo de la Prefectura de Chuxiong en la Prefectura autónoma yi de Chuxiong, en Yunnan, China, con el número de catálogo CPM C2140ZA245

facts.statement: The snout of the specimen was bent to the left due to deformation during fossilization.
facts.quote: El hocico del espécimen se dobló hacia la izquierda debido a la deformación durante la fosilización

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in purple clayey siltstone layers in Liuna village, Anlongbao town, Shuangbai County, Chuxiong Yi, about 100 kilometers south of the well-known Lufeng deposits.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto en capas de limolita púrpura lodosa localizada en la villa Liuna, en el pueblo Anlongbao, condado de Shuangbai en Chuxiong Yi, cerca de 100 kilómetros a sur de los bien conocidos depósitos de Lufeng

facts.statement: These layers belong to the Fengjiahe Formation, which is tentatively dated to the Hettangian of the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Estas capas han sido reconocidas como pertenecientes a la Formación Fengjiahe, la cual ha sido datada tentativamente a la época del Hettangiense en el Jurásico Inferior

facts.statement: In 2017, the type and only known species of the genus Shuangbaisaurus, S. anlongbaoensis, was formally described and named by Wang Guo-Fu, You Hai-Lu, Pan Shi-Gang, and Wang Tao.
facts.quote: En 2017, la especie tipo y única conocida para el género Shuangbaisaurus, S. anlongbaoensis, fue descrita y nombrada formalmente por Wang Guo-Fu, You Hai-Lu, Pan Shi-Gang y Wang Tao

facts.statement: The genus name refers to Shuangbai County, while the species name refers to Anlongbao village.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se refiere al condado de Shuangbai, mientras que el nombre de la especiese refiere al pueblo de Anlongbao

facts.statement: In a 2019 conference summary, Philip Currie and colleagues suggested that specimen CPM C2140ZA245 falls within the variation range of specimens assigned to Sinosaurus triassicus.
facts.quote: En un resumen de la conferencia de 2019, Philip Currie y sus colegas sugirieron que CPM C2140ZA245 se encontraba dentro del rango de variación de los especímenes asignados a Sinosaurus triassicus

facts.statement: After Dilophosaurus and Sinosaurus, Shuangbaisaurus is the third large theropod known to have had a pair of crests on its skull.
facts.quote: Tras Dilophosaurus y Sinosaurus, Shuangbaisaurus es el tercer terópodo grande que se sabe que tuvo un par de crestas en su cráneo

facts.statement: Shuangbaisaurus appears to have been generally very similar to the approximately contemporary Sinosaurus.
facts.quote: Shuangbaisaurus parece haber sido en general muy parecido al aproximadamente contemporáneo Sinosaurus

facts.statement: However, the vertical groove separating the premaxilla from the maxilla, which appears present in Shuangbaisaurus, was identified as a distinctive feature of Sinosaurus by Matthew Carrano and colleagues in 2012.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el surco vertical que separa el premaxilar del maxilar, el cual parece estar presente en Shuangbaisaurus, fue señalado como una característica distintiva de Sinosaurus por Matthew Carrano y colaboradores en 2012

facts.statement: This complicates the classification as a new genus made by Wang et al.
facts.quote: lo cual complica la clasificación como un nuevo género hecha por Wang et al.

facts.statement: Alongside Shuangbaisaurus, various dinosaurs from the Fengjiahe Formation have been found, including sauropodomorphs such as Chinshakiangosaurus chunghoensis, Lufengosaurus sp., Yimenosaurus youngi, and Yunnanosaurus huangi.
facts.quote: Además de Shuangbaisaurus, se han hallado varios dinosaurios originarios de la Formación Fengjiahe. Estos incluyen a los sauropodomorfos Chinshakiangosaurus chunghoensis (un posible saurópodo), Lufengosaurus sp., Yimenosaurus youngi, y Yunnanosaurus huangi (un espécimen juvenil, el cual fue descubierto también en Shuangbai)

facts.statement: Ostracods of the genus Darwinula have also been found in the area.
facts.quote: También se han hallado ostrácodos del género Darwinula

facts.statement: A diverse fauna represented by trackways has been found in the Fengjiahe Formation deposits, including ichnotaxa such as Eubrontes platypus, Grallator limnosus, Paracoelurosaurichnus monax, Schizograllator xiaohebaensis, Youngichnus xiyangensis, and Zhengichnus jinningensis.
facts.quote: Se ha encontrado asimismo una diversa fauna representada en icnitas en los depósitos de la Formación Fengjiahe, incluyendo a los icnotaxones Eubrontes platypus, Grallator limnosus, Paracoelurosaurichnus monax, Schizograllator xiaohebaensis, Youngichnus xiyangensis y Zhengichnus jinningensis

facts.quote: PBDB name: Shuangbaisaurus (genus), Wang et al. 2017

facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Hettangian (201.4 to 199.5 million years ago)
